questions.text:
Mum will be away on a work trip for three weeks. She says, "Three weeks is about 30,000 minutes."

Is she right? Use time calculations to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — 3 weeks = 21 days = 504 hours = about 30,240 minutes
questions.markingGuide: Student must show calculation: 3 weeks x 7 = 21 days, 21 x 24 = 504 hours, 504 x 60 = 30,240 minutes. Then state that 30,240 is about 30,000 so she is approximately right. Accept rounding explanations.

questions.text:
Dad is setting up a reading light. He needs the light arm to be tilted at an angle.

The angle between the wall and the light arm is 40°.

What is the angle between the light arm and a horizontal line going straight out from the wall?
questions.markingGuide: The angle from horizontal = 90° - 40° = 50°. Accept 50 degrees.

questions.text:
Dad jogs along a coastal path that is 3.6 km long. He checks his watch after running for 12 minutes and has covered 1200 metres.

At this rate, approximately how long will the entire jog take?

(A) 24 minutes
(B) 30 minutes
(C) 36 minutes
(D) 42 minutes
(E) 48 minutes
questions.markingGuide: 1200 m in 12 min, so 3600 m at same rate = 3600/1200 x 12 = 3 x 12 = 36 minutes. The correct answer is C.

questions.text:
Dad wants a raised planter box filled with soil. The planter box is 2.0 m long, 1.5 m wide, and 0.5 m deep.

How many cubic metres (m³) of soil are needed?
questions.markingGuide: Volume = 2.0 x 1.5 x 0.5 = 1.5 m³.

questions.text:
Mum puts 8 kilograms of wet clothes into the dryer. After tumble drying, the dry clothes weigh 0.75 times the weight they were when wet.

How much do the dry clothes weigh, in kilograms?
questions.markingGuide: 8 x 0.75 = 6 kg. Award mark for correct answer.

questions.text:
Dad notices the 200-litre compost bin is ¾ full.

How much space, in litres, is left in the bin?
questions.markingGuide: If the bin is 3/4 full, then 1/4 is empty. 200 / 4 = 50 litres left. Award mark for correct answer.

questions.text:
Tramping packs come in different sizes.

Size chart — Maximum load and volume:
• Small: Volume 40 L, Max load 12 kg
• Medium: Volume 55 L, Max load 16 kg
• Large: Volume 70 L, Max load 20 kg
• X-Large: Volume 85 L, Max load 24 kg

Rewa has 18 kg of gear and needs at least 65 litres of space.

Rewa thinks a Medium pack will be best. Do you agree? Use measurements from the table to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: No — Rewa has 18 kg of gear (too heavy for Medium at 16 kg max) and needs 65 L of space (Medium only has 55 L). She needs Large.
questions.markingGuide: Student must compare Rewa's needs against the table. Weight 18 kg exceeds Medium's max load (16 kg). Volume 65 L exceeds Medium's volume (55 L). Large (70 L, 20 kg) fits both requirements. Accept answers that correctly use data from the table.

questions.text:
The price of a wetsuit is usually $180. On sale, you get 20% off.

What is the sale price of the wetsuit?

A barbecue has different heat settings with recommended uses:

(i) High: Searing steaks
(ii) Medium-High: Grilling sausages and burgers
(iii) Medium: Cooking chicken pieces through
(iv) Low: Warming buns and bread
(v) Very Low: Melting cheese on top

You want to cook chicken pieces all the way through.

Tick the best heat setting for cooking chicken.
questions.markingGuide: Student reads the guide to find the setting for cooking chicken through. The correct answer is (iii) Medium.

questions.text:
Three different surfboards have these specifications:

Board A: Weight 3.2 kg, Length 6'2", Price $480
Board B: Weight 4.5 kg, Length 7'0", Price $390
Board C: Weight 2.8 kg, Length 6'0", Price $620

Is it true to say 'Lighter boards cost more, but are shorter than heavier boards'? Use numbers from any two boards to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Partially true — Board C is lightest and most expensive, and shortest. Board B is heaviest and cheapest, and longest.
questions.markingGuide: Student must compare data from two boards and use specific numbers (weight, length, and/or price) to support or refute the claim. Accept any correct comparison with supporting numbers.

questions.text:
While tramping, the temperature at the summit was measured at 8.6°C. The temperature at the base of the mountain was measured at -2.4°C.

What is the difference between 8.6°C and -2.4°C?

A chart shows the number of visitors to a ski field each month during 2023 and 2024.

Visitors per month: Jan = 80, Feb = 60, Mar = 40, Apr = 30, May = 120, Jun = 350, Jul = 480, Aug = 420, Sep = 200, Oct = 90, Nov = 50, Dec = 70.

Note: June, July, and August are winter (ski season). December, January, and February are summer.

'More people visit the ski field in cold months than warm months.'

Do you agree? Use information from the data to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — visits peak in winter months (Jun-Aug: 350, 480, 420) and are lowest in summer (Dec-Feb: 70, 80, 60)
questions.markingGuide: Student must refer to specific data to support their answer. They should identify that cold months (Jun-Aug) show much higher visitor numbers and warm months (Dec-Feb) show lower numbers, using approximate figures.

questions.text:
You want to visit the community market on a Sunday after 11 a.m. You prefer a market that is busy.

Market A: busiest at 8-10 a.m. (about 300 people), quieter after noon (about 100 people).
Market B: quiet in the morning, busiest at 11:30 a.m. - 1 p.m. (about 350 people).

Which market should you visit, and what time should you go? Use information from the data to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Market B at 11:30 a.m. — it has the most people (350) after 11 a.m.
questions.markingGuide: Student must name a market and a time after 11 a.m., and use the data to justify their choice by referring to the number of people.

questions.text:
The price of manuka honey is $6.40 per kilogram.

How much will it cost for a jar of honey that weighs 500 grams? Round your answer to the nearest cent.

A stack of six crates is 150 cm tall. A stack of three crates is 90 cm tall. Each crate sits inside the one below it.

When one extra crate is added to either stack, how much does the total height increase by? Write your answer in centimetres.
questions.markingGuide: The difference between 6 crates (150 cm) and 3 crates (90 cm) is 60 cm for 3 extra crates. So each extra crate adds 60 / 3 = 20 cm. Award mark for 20 cm.

questions.text:
A 2 kg bag of flour costs $5.60, a 1 kg bag of the same flour costs $3.50, and a 500 g bag of the same flour costs $2.20.

Which bag of flour is the cheapest per 100 grams? Use the weights and prices to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: The 2 kg bag — $0.28 per 100 g vs $0.35 and $0.44
questions.markingGuide: Student must calculate the price per 100 g for at least two bags and identify the 2 kg bag as cheapest. 2 kg = $0.28/100 g, 1 kg = $0.35/100 g, 500 g = $0.44/100 g.

questions.text:
A tissue box has the shape of a rectangular prism (cuboid). Below are three possible nets (flat patterns).

Net (i) has 6 rectangular faces that fold into a cuboid shape.
Net (ii) has faces that overlap when folded.
Net (iii) has faces that do not connect properly.

Tick the net that would fold to make the tissue box.

(i), (ii), or (iii)
questions.markingGuide: Student must identify which net folds correctly. The correct answer is (i).

questions.text:
A tub holds 840 grams of washing powder. Each wash uses 35 grams of powder.

How many washes can be done from the 840 gram tub?
questions.markingGuide: Each wash uses 35 grams. 840 / 35 = 24 washes. Award mark for 24.

questions.text:
In an orchestra, instruments have different beat values.

Whole note = 4 beats, Half note = 2 beats, Quarter note = 1 beat, Eighth note = 1/2 beat.

Four combinations of notes are given:
(i) 2 half notes + 1 quarter note = 5 beats
(ii) 1 whole note + 2 eighth notes = 5 beats
(iii) 3 quarter notes + 2 eighth notes = 4 beats
(iv) 1 half note + 3 quarter notes + 2 eighth notes = 6 beats

Tick the combination of notes that adds together to make a total of four beats.
questions.markingGuide: Count beats: (i) 2x2 + 1 = 5, (ii) 4 + 2x0.5 = 5, (iii) 3x1 + 2x0.5 = 4, (iv) 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. The correct answer is (iii).

questions.text:
A kowhaiwhai design is drawn with several elements. Some parts of the design have mirror symmetry and some do not.

Of the following parts:
(i) The main curved line
(ii) The left and right border panels
(iii) The background shading
(iv) The outer rectangular border
(v) The central curving tendril

Tick the TWO parts of the design that have mirror symmetry.
questions.markingGuide: Student must identify the TWO parts with mirror symmetry. The border panels and outer border are symmetrical. Both must be selected for the mark.

questions.text:
On average, New Zealanders spend 780 hours per year listening to music. There are 52 weeks in one year.

How many hours per week, on average, do New Zealanders listen to music?
questions.markingGuide: 780 / 52 = 15 hours per week. Award mark for 15.

questions.text:
A class library has 200 books of different genres:

| Genre | Count |
|-------|-------|
| Fiction | 60 |
| Non-fiction | 50 |
| Graphic novels | 40 |
| Other | 50 |

If one book is picked at random, what is the probability that it will be a fiction book? Write your answer as a percentage.

The table below shows how much an artist earns per sale on different online platforms:

Platform A: $0.85 per sale
Platform B: $0.60 per sale
Platform C: $1.20 per sale
Platform D: $0.45 per sale
Platform E: $0.95 per sale

'Platform C gives artists the best deal.'

Do you agree? Use numbers from the table to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — Platform C pays $1.20 per sale, which is more than all others
questions.markingGuide: Student must use numbers from the table to support or refute the statement. They need to compare Platform C's rate ($1.20) with at least one other platform and make a clear conclusion.

graph.title: Artist Earnings per Sale by Platform

questions.text:
A survey compares how people in two age groups watch sport.

Age 15-24: Streaming 65%, TV 15%, Live at venue 8%, Radio 7%, Other 5%
Age 55-64: Streaming 20%, TV 45%, Live at venue 12%, Radio 18%, Other 5%

From the list below, tick the TWO statements that are true.

(i) Over 3/5 of 15-24 year olds use streaming.
(ii) More than 1/4 of 55-64 year olds use streaming.
(iii) Exactly 1/2 of 15-24 year olds watch on TV.
(iv) About 9/20 of 55-64 year olds watch on TV.
(v) Less than 10% of 55-64 year olds go to live events.
options: (i) Over 3/5 of 15-24 year olds use streaming
(ii) More than 1/4 of 55-64 year olds use streaming
(iii) Exactly 1/2 of 15-24 year olds watch on TV
(iv) About 9/20 of 55-64 year olds watch on TV
(v) Less than 10% of 55-64 year olds go to live events
questions.markingGuide: Check each: (i) 65% > 60% (3/5) — TRUE. (ii) 20% = 1/5, not MORE than 1/4 (25%) — FALSE. (iii) 15% is not 50% — FALSE. (iv) 45% = 9/20 — TRUE. (v) 12% > 10% — FALSE. Both (i) and (iv) must be selected.

graph.title: How People Watch Sport — by Age Group

questions.text:
An adult humpback whale is 13.5 metres long. Its calf is 4.5 metres long.

How many times longer is the adult whale than its calf?
questions.markingGuide: 13.5 / 4.5 = 3. Award mark for 3.

questions.text:
Penguins must eat between 8% and 12% of their body weight in food each day. This penguin weighs 5 kilograms.

What is the minimum amount of food this penguin must eat each day?
questions.markingGuide: Minimum is 8% of 5 kg. 8% x 5 = 0.08 x 5 = 0.4 kg. Award mark for 0.4.

questions.text:
Seals have been spotted at various locations around the coast. A map shows locations A-F with latitude and longitude grid lines.

Which location is closest to 43.5° S and 172.6° E?

These coordinates are near Christchurch. Location C is marked nearest to Christchurch on the map.

(A) Northland
(B) Waikato
(C) Canterbury
(D) Wellington
(E) Southland
(F) West Coast
questions.markingGuide: 43.5° S, 172.6° E is near Christchurch in Canterbury. The correct answer is C.

questions.text:
Whales are excellent divers. A number line shows depth from 0 metres (sea level) to 600 metres. A sperm whale typically dives to about 2/3 of this maximum depth.

Estimate the depth the sperm whale would dive to.
questions.markingGuide: 2/3 of 600 = 400 metres. Accept 380-420 metres.

questions.text:
A chart shows what seals eat at different times of the year.

Autumn/Winter diet: Fish 50%, Squid 25%, Crustaceans 15%, Other 10%.
Spring/Summer diet: Fish 30%, Squid 15%, Crustaceans 30%, Other 25%.

'In autumn and winter, seals eat mostly fish and squid.'

Do you agree? Use percentages from the data to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — fish (50%) + squid (25%) = 75%, which is three quarters of the diet
questions.markingGuide: Student must read autumn/winter percentages and add them: fish 50% + squid 25% = 75%. This is well over half, so fish and squid are the clear majority of the diet. Accept either agree or disagree if justified with specific percentages.

questions.text:
Researchers tracked seabirds from Banks Peninsula. The furthest seabird was spotted at a location that, using the map scale, is 5 scale-bar lengths from Banks Peninsula. Each scale-bar length represents 8 km.

Estimate the distance from Banks Peninsula to where the furthest seabird was spotted.
questions.markingGuide: 5 x 8 km = 40 km. Accept 35-45 km.

headers: Scale bar lengths from Banks Peninsula
